name: Distilling Step-by-Step! Outperforming Larger Language Models with Less Training Data and Smaller Model Sizes
authors: Hsieh, Li, Du, Fu, Zhou, Liu, Lee, Hsieh
problem: Fine-tuning and distilling small models both need large amounts of training data to match a prompted LLM.
mechanism: Extract the LLM's RATIONALES as additional supervision and train the small model on (input, rationale, answer) triples inside a multi-task framework - the rationale is a training signal the student gets for free from the teacher. The result is that data EFFICIENCY, not model size, becomes the binding constraint: the student needs far fewer examples because each example now carries a reasoning trace.
speedup_reported: Paper's own claim (abstract): across 4 NLP benchmarks, (1) better performance than both fine-tuning and distillation with far fewer training examples; (2) better performance than FEW-SHOT PROMPTED LLMs at substantially smaller model sizes; (3) a finetuned 770M T5 OUTPERFORMS THE FEW-SHOT PROMPTED 540B PaLM MODEL using only 80% of the available data on a benchmark, where standard finetuning of the same T5 'struggles to match even by using 100% of the dataset'. The 770M-beats-540B-on-80%-of-the-data figure is the headline and the 100%-failure of the baseline is what makes it meaningful.
